description: Frozen labeled retrieval dataset v1. DO NOT edit to improve scores — that defeats the purpose. Add a new version file instead.

corpus.title: SQLite WAL mode deadlock with multiple writers
corpus.summary: Enabling WAL mode does not prevent deadlocks when multiple processes open the same database concurrently without timeouts.
corpus.details: Attempted to run two background workers both writing to the SQLite database simultaneously. Both blocked indefinitely. Root cause: SQLite WAL still serialises writes at the database level. Fix: set a busy_timeout of 5000ms via PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 before any write.

corpus.title: FTS5 MATCH expressions must double-quote each token
corpus.summary: Raw user input passed directly to FTS5 MATCH causes OperationalError when input contains special characters like hyphens or parentheses.
corpus.details: FTS5 treats hyphens as negation operators and parentheses as grouping. User queries like 'KeyError: key-not-found' break the MATCH expression. Each token must be individually double-quoted: "KeyError" "key" "not" "found".

corpus.title: Using sqlite3 row_factory=dict breaks ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
corpus.summary: Setting conn.row_factory = lambda c, r: dict(zip([d[0] for d in c.description], r)) causes ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE clauses to fail silently.
corpus.details: Discovered during upsert testing: dict row_factory changes column ordering assumptions. Switched to sqlite3.Row which preserves column access by name without breaking conflict resolution.

corpus.title: Memory IDs are SHA256-derived from content+source for deduplication
corpus.summary: Memory entry IDs are computed as stable_id(kind, title, summary, source_ref, prefix=prefix) so that re-ingesting the same content produces the same ID.
corpus.details: Decision made 2025-03: deterministic IDs allow safe ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upserts and prevent duplicate entries across repeated ingestion runs. Changing the ID derivation formula would invalidate all existing stored IDs.

corpus.title: All embedding vectors must be L2-normalised (unit norm)
corpus.summary: Cosine similarity computation in the reranker assumes unit-norm vectors. Un-normalised vectors produce incorrect similarity scores.
corpus.details: Violated once when a custom embedder returned raw TF counts. The cosine similarity function does not re-normalise its inputs for performance reasons. Every Embedder implementation MUST return L2-normalised vectors.

corpus.title: Importing typer at module load time breaks --help latency
corpus.summary: Placing heavyweight imports (torch, sentence_transformers) at module top level increased CLI startup time from 80ms to 4200ms.
corpus.details: All optional ML dependencies must use lazy imports guarded inside functions. The CLI --help path must complete in under 200ms. Pattern: 'from oh_no_my_claudecode.embeddings.core import get_embedder' inside the function body, never at module level.

corpus.title: Pydantic BaseModel datetime fields lose timezone info on JSON round-trip
corpus.summary: datetime fields serialised with model_dump() and then parsed back may lose UTC timezone info, causing comparison bugs.
corpus.details: Use model_dump(mode='json') which serialises datetimes to ISO strings with Z suffix. Alternatively use model_dump_json() + model_validate_json(). Never use plain json.loads(model.model_dump_json()) — it returns strings, not datetime objects.

corpus.title: Using git stash in subprocess during pre-commit hook causes hook failure
corpus.summary: Running git stash inside a pre-commit hook script creates a deadlock because git already holds a lock on the index.
corpus.details: Attempted to stash unstaged changes before running type-check in the pre-commit hook. Git raised 'fatal: Unable to create .git/index.lock: File exists'. Solution: use git diff --name-only HEAD to identify changed files and lint only those.

corpus.title: CLI commands must complete in under 200ms for the happy path
corpus.summary: Any onmc command that does not require LLM calls or network access must return in under 200ms measured on a cold process start.
corpus.details: Enforced by performance tests. The limit exists because onmc is invoked from shell hooks where latency is user-visible. Heavy work must be deferred to background threads or async tasks.

corpus.title: FTS5 is preferred over LIKE scan for memory search
corpus.summary: SQLite FTS5 provides BM25-ranked full-text search with tokenisation, prefix matching, and phrase search. LIKE scan is kept as a fallback when FTS5 is unavailable.
corpus.details: Decision 2025-01: FTS5 is always preferred when available because BM25 ranking is significantly better than simple substring match for multi-keyword queries. The LIKE fallback ensures the module works with read-only SQLite builds that lack FTS5.

corpus.title: Hashing user queries before FTS lookup strips important search signal
corpus.summary: Normalising error text too aggressively (e.g. stripping all digits) removes version numbers that are critical for distinguishing between similar errors in different library versions.
corpus.details: Tried hashing the normalised query tokens to reduce FTS index size. Recall dropped 40%. Root cause: version numbers like '3.11' are important distinguishers. Reverted normalisation to only strip line numbers and addresses, not all numeric tokens.

corpus.title: SQLiteStorage.initialize() is not idempotent without IF NOT EXISTS
corpus.summary: Calling initialize() twice on the same database raises 'table already exists' unless DDL uses IF NOT EXISTS.
corpus.details: All CREATE TABLE and CREATE INDEX statements in the migration chain must use IF NOT EXISTS. The migration runner tracks applied versions in a schema_version table to avoid re-running migrations.

corpus.title: Running pytest with --forked breaks SQLite in-memory databases
corpus.summary: pytest-forked forks the process after SQLite connections are opened, causing the child to inherit a corrupted connection state.
corpus.details: SQLite connections are not fork-safe. Tests that use in-memory databases (:memory:) must open new connections inside each test function. Removed --forked from pytest configuration; use tmp_path fixture for isolation instead.

corpus.title: Embeddings are optional and gated by ONMC_EMBEDDER env var
corpus.summary: The HashNgramEmbedder is always available as a zero-dependency default. Real ML embedders (fastembed, sentence-transformers) are only loaded when ONMC_EMBEDDER is set.
corpus.details: Decision: never require GPU or ML dependencies at install time. embeddings_enabled() returns False when ONMC_EMBEDDER is unset. The reranker degrades gracefully to lexical-only when embeddings are disabled.

corpus.title: HashNgramEmbedder returns zero vector for empty strings
corpus.summary: Passing an empty string or whitespace-only string to HashNgramEmbedder.embed() returns a zero vector [0.0]*dim, not a unit vector.
corpus.details: Cosine similarity of zero vector with any other vector is undefined (division by zero). The reranker must guard against zero-vector queries and documents before computing similarity. Check: math.sqrt(sum(v*v for v in vector)) > 0.

corpus.title: Storing raw Python tracebacks in memory summary field truncates at 500 chars
corpus.summary: The summary field has a soft limit enforced by the ingest layer. Long tracebacks stored in summary are silently truncated, losing the 'most recent call last' section.
corpus.details: Full tracebacks belong in the details field. Summary should contain only the exception type and message (first line). Ingest layer enforces: len(summary) <= 500. Details field allows up to 4000 chars.

corpus.title: Memory confidence score must stay in [0.0, 1.0]
corpus.summary: MemoryEntry.confidence is validated by Pydantic to be in [0.0, 1.0]. Values outside this range raise ValidationError at construction time.
corpus.details: Invariant enforced by Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0). Any computation that derives confidence from external signals (e.g. git blame age, test pass rate) must clamp the result before constructing MemoryEntry.

corpus.title: typer==0.12 changed the signature of add_typer, breaking existing plugins
corpus.summary: typer 0.12 deprecated the 'callback' parameter in add_typer and raises a deprecation warning that becomes an error in 0.13.
corpus.details: All add_typer() calls must use invoke_without_command=True instead of callback for the parent command group. Detected when CI started failing on typer upgrade. Pin to typer>=0.9,<0.14 in pyproject.toml to avoid silent breakage.

corpus.title: Using threading.Lock for SQLite connection pool causes deadlock under pytest-xdist
corpus.summary: A module-level threading.Lock guarding the SQLite connection pool deadlocks when pytest-xdist runs tests in the same process with multiple threads.
corpus.details: Replaced connection pool with per-call contextmanager that opens and closes SQLite connections. The performance cost is acceptable for a CLI tool that does not hold connections across requests.

corpus.title: CLI command names must be lowercase with hyphens, not underscores
corpus.summary: Typer maps Python function names with underscores to CLI names with hyphens by default. We follow this convention explicitly.
corpus.details: Decision: function def record_memory maps to 'onmc record-memory'. Never override name= in @app.command() to use underscores. This ensures consistent tab-completion behaviour across shells.

corpus.title: HDBSCAN with min_cluster_size=3 over-segments small corpora
corpus.summary: Setting min_cluster_size=3 on a corpus of fewer than 30 points produces 15+ singleton clusters (noise points), defeating the clustering purpose.
corpus.details: For corpora under 50 points, min_cluster_size should be at least max(5, corpus_size // 10). Discovered during a behaviours pipeline run on a 22-span bench that produced 18 clusters of size 1.

corpus.title: pathlib.Path.stat() raises FileNotFoundError on dangling symlinks
corpus.summary: Path.stat() follows symlinks and raises FileNotFoundError when the symlink target does not exist, even though Path.exists() returns True for the symlink itself.
corpus.details: Use Path.lstat() to stat the symlink inode itself, or Path.is_symlink() before calling stat(). Discovered when ingesting a repository with broken symlinks in node_modules.

corpus.title: Background task results must be written before process exit
corpus.summary: Any background thread or task that writes to SQLite must be joined before the process exits, or writes may be lost without error.
corpus.details: Python's atexit handlers run after daemon threads are killed. All SQLite writes from background threads must complete before main thread exits. Use threading.Event or Queue with a sentinel to drain background workers.

corpus.title: Staleness labels are assigned at read time, not write time
corpus.summary: Memory staleness (fresh/stale/orphaned/unanchored) is computed when memories are listed, not when they are stored.
corpus.details: Decision: computing staleness at write time would require re-writing all memories whenever the git graph changes. Instead, staleness is derived from the memory source_ref against the current git state each time list_memories() is called.

corpus.title: Using os.getenv inside Pydantic validator causes test isolation failures
corpus.summary: Pydantic validators that call os.getenv() read the real environment at validation time, making tests that mock environment variables flaky.
corpus.details: Tests that monkeypatch os.environ must patch before the Pydantic model is constructed. Alternatively, pass env values as explicit parameters to the model rather than reading from os.getenv inside the validator.

corpus.title: Rich console.print with markup=False required for user content
corpus.summary: Passing user-controlled strings to rich console.print() without markup=False can cause Rich markup injection if the string contains square brackets.
corpus.details: A memory title containing '[deprecated]' was rendered as an empty string because Rich interpreted it as an unknown markup tag and silently dropped it. Always use markup=False for any string that comes from user data or the database.

corpus.title: Concurrent pytest workers corrupt shared SQLite database
corpus.summary: Running pytest-xdist with 4 workers all writing to the same tmp_path/db.sqlite causes SQLITE_BUSY and data corruption.
corpus.details: Each xdist worker must use its own database file. Use the worker_id fixture from pytest-xdist to suffix the database path: db_path = tmp_path / f'onmc-{worker_id}.sqlite'. Confirmed fix: tests pass reliably with -n4.

corpus.title: Token overlap scoring normalises by query token count, not document token count
corpus.summary: Relevance score = |query_tokens ∩ doc_tokens| / |query_tokens|, not IDF-weighted.
corpus.details: Decision: normalising by query token count ensures that a short precise query with high overlap beats a long noisy query with incidental matches. Document length does not penalise or reward long memories.

corpus.title: Pickle-caching embedding vectors between sessions breaks on model upgrade
corpus.summary: Caching embedding vectors as pickle files keyed only by memory ID causes stale vectors after the embedder model is upgraded.
corpus.details: Cache keys must include the embedder_id (e.g. 'hash-ngram-v1', 'fastembed-v1'). The memory_vectors table in SQLite stores (memory_id, embedder_id, content_hash, vector). Cache invalidation on model upgrade is automatic because embedder_id changes.

corpus.title: uv run and python -m pytest disagree on sys.path when using src layout
corpus.summary: uv run pytest finds the package because uv installs it editably, but python -m pytest may not find it if the virtual env is not activated.
corpus.details: Always run tests with 'uv run python -m pytest' or 'uv run pytest', never with bare 'python -m pytest' in a src-layout project. The src/ directory is only on sys.path when the package is installed editably.

corpus.title: generate-cli-reference.py must be regenerated after any CLI change
corpus.summary: docs/cli-reference.md is auto-generated from the CLI surface. Any PR that adds/removes/renames a command must regenerate it or CI quality check fails.
corpus.details: Script: scripts/generate-cli-reference.py --check verifies the current docs match the CLI. Run: python scripts/generate-cli-reference.py to regenerate. This file is a merge conflict magnet — serialize command-adding PRs.

corpus.title: Storing memory tags as comma-separated string loses tags containing commas
corpus.summary: Tags like 'foo, bar' stored as a comma-separated string in SQLite cannot be reliably split back because some tags contain commas.
corpus.details: Tags are now stored as a JSON array in the tags_json column. The FTS index over tags concatenates them with spaces for search. Migration v3 backfilled all existing tag columns to JSON format.

corpus.title: Memory confidence decays exponentially with age, halving every 90 days
corpus.summary: The decay factor formula is: max(DECAY_FLOOR=0.3, 2^(-age_days / DECAY_HALF_LIFE=90)). Positive feedback reduces effective age.
corpus.details: Decision: memories should lose confidence over time to prevent stale data from dominating search results. Positive user feedback (onmc memory confirm) halves the effective age. The 0.3 floor prevents old-but-important memories from disappearing entirely.

corpus.title: ruff check --fix modifies files that are staged but not committed
corpus.summary: Running ruff --fix in a pre-commit hook modifies staged files on disk without re-staging them, causing 'partially staged' warnings in git.
corpus.details: Pre-commit hooks that auto-fix must re-stage modified files with 'git add <files>' after fixing, or use pre-commit framework's auto-stage feature. Without re-staging, the commit contains the unfixed version.

corpus.title: Using asyncio.run() inside a Typer command breaks event loop on Python 3.10
corpus.summary: Calling asyncio.run() from within a Typer command raises RuntimeError: 'Event loop is already running' on Python 3.10 when the CLI is invoked from an async context.
corpus.details: Typer does not run commands in an async context, but some test harnesses do. Use anyio.from_thread.run_sync() or restructure the command to be synchronous. Confirmed on Python 3.10.12 and 3.11.4.

corpus.title: SQLiteStorage must be initialised before first use
corpus.summary: Calling any SQLiteStorage method before initialize() raises 'no such table: memories' because the schema has not been created.
corpus.details: initialize() creates all tables and runs migrations. It is safe to call multiple times (idempotent). Tests must call storage.initialize() in setup. Production code initialises in the service constructor.
